comment: TEMPLATE. Copy this file to private/owner-data-patterns.owner.json and replace every value with your own before building. The private/ destination is local and ignored by Git. This file lists the strings that identify YOU, and the ship gate refuses to build until it exists -- a privacy guard with no identity to look for is a guard that passes everything.
matching: Entries are matched as raw bytes anywhere in any shipped file, case-insensitively by default. Set caseSensitive: true where case carries meaning.
ownership: The local private/owner-data-patterns.owner.json belongs to whoever set it up. A copied, cached, or otherwise incorrect profile can make a guard scan for a stranger's identity while YOUR name ships, so the gate also requires at least one pattern there to relate to the OS account running the build (case-insensitive substring, either direction). Leaving these placeholder values in place will not pass. On CI or a shared build machine whose account name legitimately differs, set MC_IDENTITY_PROFILE_ACCOUNT to the account name the local profile describes -- it renames the account being checked, it does not switch the check off.

patterns.note: The account name in your home-directory paths.
Your name as prose. Path-shaped checks will not catch a name in shipped UI text.
Surname alone, for text that omits the given name.
Work/school/vendor account identifiers. These are neither names nor paths, so nothing else catches them.
Your private LAN range, if any hostname or address could be baked into a build.
